key_terms: Similar figures: Figures possessing the same shape but not necessarily the same size. All congruent figures are similar, but similar figures are not necessarily congruent.

Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT / Thales' Theorem): If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides in distinct points, it divides the two sides in the same ratio.
Converse of BPT: If a line divides any two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, the line must be parallel to the third side.
1. AAA (or AA) Similarity Criterion: If corresponding angles of two triangles are equal, corresponding sides are proportional, making triangles similar.
2. SSS Similarity Criterion: If corresponding sides of two triangles are in the same ratio, corresponding angles are equal, making triangles similar.
3. SAS Similarity Criterion: If one angle of a triangle equals one angle of another and the including sides are proportional, the triangles are similar.
